title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 75
paragraphs: The Thracians served wearing fox-skins on their heads and tunics over their bodies, with multicolored cloaks thrown loosely over them; on their feet and lower legs they wore fawn-skin boots. In addition they had javelins, small round shields, and short daggers. After they had crossed over into Asia, these men came to be called Bithynians; but formerly, as they themselves say, they were called Strymonians, since they had lived by the river Strymon; they say they were driven out of their old homes by the Teucrians and Mysians. The commander of the Thracians who lived in Asia was Bassakes son of Artabanus.

They carried small shields of raw oxhide, and each man carried two hunting-spears of Lycian make. On their heads they wore bronze helmets to which the ears and horns of an ox were attached, also in bronze, with crests on top; and their lower legs were wrapped with strips of red cloth. Among these men there is an oracle of Ares.
